summary: Enterprise customer reporting elevated 429s during burst traffic on hot route; questions about per-route limits + Retry-After guidance
content:
Issue summary
- Customer (Northstar Capital) reports elevated HTTP 429 responses during a burst in traffic to their primary chat route.
- Customer is an enterprise Hosted API account and expects enterprise priority behavior during bursts.
- Customer asked:
  1) Are these 429s a quota issue vs rate limit vs capacity protection?
  2) Should they rely on Retry-After? They saw missing/inconsistent Retry-After values.
  3) What is the recommended retry strategy and max concurrency?

Impact
- Time window: 2025-01-17 16:10–16:55 UTC (reported). Customer indicated sustained 429 rate of ~8–15% for ~35–45 minutes.
- End-user impact: degraded completion success rate; client retried aggressively and saw occasional latency spikes.
- Scope: limited to a single tenant + one hot route in us-east.

Environment
- Prod, region us-east
- Endpoint/route: POST /v1/chat/completions
- Models: redwood-llama-70b-instruct (primary), redwood-qwen2.5-72b-instruct (fallback observed)

Customer-provided symptoms
- Example response:
  - Status: 429
  - Body: {"error":{"type":"rate_limit","message":"Over capacity for this route","code":"OVER_CAPACITY"}}
  - They noted Retry-After header was sometimes missing; when present they saw small values (0–1s) and retried immediately with high concurrency.

Initial triage notes (Support/SRE)
- Hypothesis A: per-route rate limit burst cap triggered at gateway for tenant+route+region key.
- Hypothesis B: capacity protection backpressure triggered (router enterprise lane admission + queue depth thresholds).
- Hypothesis C: client retry storm amplified throttling, making it appear worse.

Investigation (what we checked)
1) Logs / request sampling
- Sample request IDs provided by customer:
  - rwreq_01HTZ9D3K4P6C3QW8F7C9J1M2A
  - rwreq_01HTZ9E0B1W0QF9GQK7Y2E5J3N
- Confirmed 429s are generated at gateway and router depending on reason code; this incident showed mostly gateway throttles (route rate limit) plus some router admission throttles during peak.

2) Dashboards
- Hot-route protection dashboard (us-east) showed elevated prefill saturation + queue depth spikes around 16:20–16:40 UTC.
- Enterprise lane health was OK (no evidence of enterprise lane starvation), but overall capacity dipped (consistent with INC-2025-01-17-us-east-capacity-dip).
- Throttled_count for tenant key increased sharply; top dimension was route=chat.completions and tier=enterprise.

3) Policy/config review
- Verified customer’s route key matched the intended policy key (tenant_id + route_id + region).
- Confirmed per-route burst limit was set to default enterprise hot-route baseline for Hosted API, but their burst exceeded the configured burst tokens/sec assumptions.

Findings
- Primary driver: burst traffic exceeded configured per-route rate limit for this tenant/route in us-east.
- Contributing factor: client retry behavior was effectively immediate and highly concurrent. When Retry-After was absent, their SDK fell back to immediate retry (no jitter) and increased concurrency, amplifying throttling.
- Secondary: during the same window, us-east experienced a capacity dip; router admission control (capacity protection) produced some 429s with over-capacity semantics as backpressure increased.
- Retry-After inconsistency: we saw a mix of 429 sources (gateway vs router). Gateway responses consistently included Retry-After; router throttles were missing Retry-After on a subset of paths (known gap addressed by standardization work).

Customer guidance provided
- Recommended behavior:
  - Treat 429 as retryable.
  - Respect Retry-After when present.
  - If Retry-After missing, use exponential backoff with jitter; cap retries; do not increase concurrency in response to 429.
  - Consider a client-side concurrency limiter per region.
- We provided suggested defaults for their workload:
  - base backoff: 250ms
  - max backoff: 5s
  - jitter: full jitter
  - max retry attempts: 3–5 (depending on end-user tolerance)

Mitigation applied (temporary)
- Increased per-route burst allowance for Northstar Capital in us-east for POST /v1/chat/completions (timeboxed 7 days) to reduce 429 rate during known peak hours.
- Asked customer to deploy updated retry logic (respect Retry-After; add jitter; cap concurrency) before we make the limit increase permanent.

Resolution
- 429 rate returned to baseline after customer reduced concurrency and after the regional capacity dip resolved.
- Temporary burst-limit increase applied; customer confirmed 429s dropped to <1% on next day’s peak.

Follow-ups / next steps
- Engineering follow-up: ensure Retry-After is standardized across gateway + router throttles and include reason codes consistently.
- Support follow-up: send customer-facing guidance snippet for 429 handling and confirm their SDK behavior.

Owner(s)
- Support: Dev Patel
- SRE consulted: Rafael Mendes
- Product consulted: Lauren Bishop (enterprise expectations) / Nikhil Sharma (Hosted semantics)

Attachments/links
- Incident: INC-2025-01-17-us-east-capacity-dip
- Runbook: overload-throttling-and-priority-routing-response
- Related work: PRs for standardizing 429 payloads + Retry-After; dashboards for throttling/lane health

2025-01-17 16:34 UTC — Liam O'Rourke (Reporter)
Customer (Northstar) escalated via TAM channel: seeing 8–15% 429s on POST /v1/chat/completions in us-east. They believe they are in the enterprise lane and expected protection during burst. They also report Retry-After header missing in some cases. Request IDs shared in ticket body.

2025-01-17 16:48 UTC — Dev Patel (Assignee)
Acknowledged. Pulling gateway/router logs for provided request IDs and checking hot-route dashboards. Initial guess: per-route RL + regional capacity dip. Looping in SRE.

2025-01-17 17:05 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE)
Checked throttling dashboards: spike aligns with broader us-east capacity dip (INC-2025-01-17-us-east-capacity-dip). Enterprise lane looks healthy but overall backpressure rose; some throttles from router admission. Most 429s appear gateway-side route RL. Need to confirm Retry-After behavior per source.

2025-01-17 17:22 UTC — Amara Diallo
Gateway 429s should always include Retry-After; if missing, likely router-generated (or older path). If customer sees mixed behavior, they are probably getting both sources. We have standardization work in flight.

2025-01-17 17:40 UTC — Dev Patel
Sent customer guidance draft: respect Retry-After; if missing, exponential backoff + jitter; cap retries; do not scale concurrency upward on 429. Asked for their current retry/concurrency settings and whether they are using multiple regions.

2025-01-18 09:10 UTC — Customer (via Liam O'Rourke)
They were doing immediate retry up to 10 attempts and increasing concurrency during failures (client-side auto-scaler). They can change this within 48h. They request temporary limit bump for Monday peak.

2025-01-18 10:02 UTC — Rafael Mendes
OK with timeboxed limit bump if we can apply tenant+route+region override. Recommend 7 days and reassess once client retry logic is fixed.

2025-01-18 10:30 UTC — Dev Patel
Applied temporary per-route burst increase for tenant in us-east (valid through 2025-01-25). Confirmed with SRE that this won’t impact fleet safety due to enterprise reservation and guardrails.

2025-01-19 15:12 UTC — Liam O'Rourke
Customer confirmed Retry-After now present on most 429s; still seeing occasional missing header. They will roll out updated retry logic (jitter + cap) today.

2025-01-20 11:05 UTC — Dev Patel
Customer peak test: 429 rate <1% and no user-visible outage. Remaining missing Retry-After cases appear router-side; tracking via linked work (standardized throttling responses). Marking ticket resolved; leaving follow-up notes in linked issues.
resolution: Resolved with temporary per-route burst limit increase (timeboxed) and customer-side retry/concurrency changes; identified mixed 429 sources (gateway vs router) causing inconsistent Retry-After, tracked as follow-up in standardization work.
